chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

In the book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'The expiation for the egg of the sandgrouse is like that for the egg of the ostrich.' And when the person in ihram breaks the egg of the sanctuary dove, he is liable for its value, according to what we have previously mentioned. Also indicating this is what has been narrated:

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.حَمَامِ الْحَرَمِ: Sanctuary dove (specifically the doves of Mecca)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking a sandgrouse or sanctuary dove egg while in ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific monetary compensation (qimah) for breaking bird eggs during ihram, equating the sandgrouse egg's penalty to that of the ostrich, a detail rooted in the economic valuation practices of early Islamic jurists. It further specifies that breaking a sanctuary dove's egg incurs its market value, illustrating the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise financial restitution for accidental transgressions within the sacred precincts (Haram).
